meta_description: Cryptographic inventory and post-quantum migration plan — 100% of the crypto estate mapped in six weeks and the migration sequence signed by the board

blocks.x: Cryptographic inventory and post-quantum migration plan, 100% of the crypto estate mapped in six weeks and the migration sequence signed by the board

Identity withheld, a digital-only challenger bank with no branches and no mainframe, which sounds like a head start until you count the cryptographic surfaces in a mobile-first stack. Figures are the client's own, shared with permission.

The baseline diagnostic mapped before it promised: 214 distinct cryptographic dependencies across mobile, API, HSM and vendor stacks, and no owner for 41 of them. Quantum risk was real but unsequenced, every vendor roadmap assumed someone else would move first.
Migration planning stalled on a circular question: which systems move first when everything depends on everything. The bank needed an order of battle, not another threat briefing.

We ran the crypto inventory as code: every key, certificate and library enumerated, classified by quantum vulnerability and mapped to its owning service; harvest-now-decrypt-later exposure ranked by data lifetime; and the migration sequence planned in dependency order with crypto-agility gates in the delivery platform so new code cannot reintroduce vulnerable primitives.

Start with the diagnostic, not the contract: the same diagnostic that baselined this program takes two weeks, and a scoped proposal follows only if the delta justifies it.
